claim.quote: The energy spectrum extends beyond 10^{20} eV and the energy gap between the highest energy event and the others is being filled up with recently observed events.

date.note: arXiv v1 date; published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 81, 1163 (1998).

name: AGASA spectrum extends beyond the GZK cutoff
notes: AGASA's own results page gives the published spectrum's epoch as Feb. 17, 1990 to Jul. 31, 2002 for the later, extended data set (Takeda et al. 2003, arXiv:astro-ph/0209422).

official_url.quote: Extension of the Cosmic-Ray Energy Spectrum Beyond the Predicted Greisen-Zatsepin-Kuz'min Cutoff

summary.plain: AGASA's array of ground detectors in Japan measured the cosmic-ray spectrum above 10^18.5 eV and found it continuing beyond 10^20 eV, where a cutoff had been predicted. The collaboration said the spectrum suggested no cutoff, or a new component beyond it.
summary.technical: Energy spectrum above 10^18.5 eV from AGASA data from February 1990 to October 1997; extends beyond 10^20 eV, the shape suggesting absence of the 2.7 K (GZK) cutoff or a new component beyond it. Later HiRes (2007) reported the suppression at 6 × 10¹⁹ eV.

title: Extension of the Cosmic-Ray Energy Spectrum Beyond the Predicted Greisen-Zatsepin-Kuz'min Cutoff
why_it_matters: The abstract says the spectral shape suggests the absence of the 2.7 K cutoff in the energy spectrum or a possible presence of a new component beyond it, which made the GZK question a central puzzle until HiRes and Auger reported a suppression.
